```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's demand evidence matches its payer. The sourced quotes come from individuals saying existing transcription tools are 'too expensive' for personal voice-to-text, which is exactly who A would charge. Idea B's sourced demand quotes all come from people helping elderly parents, not from support-team managers, the payer B would actually bill.",
    "The 90-day bar is one paying customer, and A has less friction getting there. It is self-serve and costs a few dollars, and it can launch in the same communities where the sourced complaints appear (r/digitaljournaling, r/selfpublish). B's B2B buyers likely expect SOC 2, GDPR/DPA or HIPAA readiness before a pilot, which by B's own brief takes longer than six weeks to build credibly.",
    "Both ideas face free substitutes. A competes with MacWhisper's one-time purchase, which is sourced. B competes with Microsoft Quick Assist and JoinByKey, also sourced. A's free-alternative threat is narrower: A's brief gives no URLs for its claims about a free Google app and Untold bundling, so under the rules those count as missing. B's free-alternative threat is fully sourced.",
    "A's sourced competitors (Lessrec, Speechnotes, TranscribeBee) show that individuals already pay for cheap pay-per-minute transcription. That is direct evidence a consumer will pay something. B has no sourced evidence of a small support team paying for a cheaper screen-viewing tool."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's claim that the pain is validated from the support-team side rests on vendor marketing of '41% faster resolution, 47% higher first-contact resolution,' which the brief gives without any source. Every sourced demand quote comes from family caregivers, a segment B's own brief says resists paying and defaults to free tools. So there is effectively no sourced evidence that B's actual payer wants this product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. A is a crowded, commoditizing market with weak pricing power, and its brief offers no differentiation. It wins mainly because B's evidence does not connect to B's payer and because B faces compliance gating. A's one-time purchase alternative, MacWhisper, is also a real risk: the seed thread's poster adopted it instead of paying per minute. Neither brief shows strong willingness-to-pay evidence."
}
```
